summary: Khenpo Dazer worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He served as a teacher at both the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and Śrī Siṃha Shedra.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khenpo Gangshar studied at Shechen Monastery under Khyentse Ozer, Shechen Kongtrul, and Karsé Kongtrul. He served as senior teacher at Shechen Monastery and founding dean at Surmang Monastery around 1957–1958.
Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under multiple teachers, including Khenchen Dazer around 1951 and Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima from around 1951 to 1955.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958) and under teachers including the 8th Traleg Rinpoche and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught at Rumtek Monastery (1967) and was abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra (1978).
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche studied under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Bokar Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.
Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang studied under numerous masters, including Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen (~1897–1901) and Shenphen Nangwa (~1903–1905).
Khenpo Nüden studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1960–1981). He served as principal shedra teacher at Rumtek Monastery and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970), and at the University of Virginia (~1973–1974).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, and Shenphen Nangwa. He held teaching posts at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Working in Tibetology and other fields, Khyenrab Norbu studied under teachers including Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang around 1896, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Ki-yong Rhi worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding an attested post at Dongguk University in 1983 and serving as professor emeritus there as attested in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Otago, supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others in 2013.

A philosopher who studied at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo, and University of Freiburg, he was an assistant (1911–1918) and professor (1923–1945) at Tokyo, a dean at Hokkaido (1947; 1950–1951), and professor at Chuo (1951–1958).
Kien T. Le is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied for an MDiv at Harvard University (2023–2026) and was a PhD and graduate student at Indiana University Bloomington in 2026.
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at Harvard University, and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Kim Knott held posts at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).
